subject: Dedicated cluster sizing — Neurolytics pilot (traffic stitch plan)
messages:
From: Elliot Porter <elliot@neurolytics.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing help for Dedicated cluster — Neurolytics pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re getting ready to commit to a short pilot and need a pre-sales sizing sketch so our infra team can provision a staging VPC. High level:
- Expected pilot duration: 6 weeks (starting mid-Aug)
- Peak TPS: ~200 requests/sec for embedding and chat endpoints (combined)
- Typical concurrent sessions during peak: ~70-90 active sessions
- Prompt mix: 60% short prompts (<=150 tokens), 30% medium (150-600 tokens), 10% long (600-1,400 tokens)
- Average response length target: ~600 tokens for chat, ~64 tokens for embeddings
- Model target: Open Llama variant (we’re flexible if there are cost/latency tradeoffs)

I attached a CSV with a 48-hour sample trace (sample_traffic_profile.csv) — it contains timestamped request types and token counts. Our main asks: a queued rough fleet-scaling recommendation (GPU count & type) and any immediate blockers (KV cache sizing, session pooling advice).

Also, our security/compliance lead will need a list of what telemetry Redwood collects during the pilot (token-level telemetry, logs retention). Can you include that?

Cheers,
Elliot Porter
Head of Platform — Neurolytics
elliot@neurolytics.ai
[Attachment: sample_traffic_profile.csv (text/csv)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Porter <elliot@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help for Dedicated cluster — Neurolytics pilot

Hi Elliot — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the trace — that helps a lot. Quick clarifying questions so our sizing is actionable:

1) Session model: are sessions long-lived (user opens a chat and keeps it live) or short/ephemeral (request-per-interaction)? If long-lived, do they reuse KV cache across requests?
2) Prefix caching: do you expect many repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts/templates) or highly unique prompts per user?
3) Latency SLO: target p95 and p99 for chat generation (e.g., p95 <= 600ms)?
4) Burst behavior: besides the 48-hour sample, do you have anticipated marketing-driven spikes (2–4x baseline) and how long do those bursts last?
5) Tokens: the CSV uses tokenized counts — confirm whether those are post-tokenizer for the model you expect to use.
6) Data residency & logs: we’ll prepare a one-pager on telemetry retention (what’s collected, retention windows, and encryption at rest/in transit). Is it OK if we share that as part of the preflight packet?

Deliverables we’ll produce after answers:
- A concise fleet stitch plan (GPU SKUs, starting counts, warm pool sizing, recommended autoscale thresholds)
- Cache/KV sizing guidance and session pool recipes
- A short SLO vs cost tradeoff table (latency targets mapped to GPU/multiplexing options)

I attached a short questionnaire that helps automate the estimate (redwood_preflight_questionnaire_v1.pdf). If you can return that with the answers and a representative 72-hour trace we’ll lock the initial numbers.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the questionnaire? Ben and Karthik will join from infra.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_preflight_questionnaire_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help for Dedicated cluster — Neurolytics pilot

Looping in a quick engineering read: based on Elliot’s initial numbers (200 req/s peak, heavy medium/long responses) my pragmatic starting sketch is:

- Baseline: 4 x H100-80GB (serving optimized) with per-node multiplexing for embedding endpoints; reserve a warm pool of 1 node for failover.
- If you need p95 < 400ms for chat gen at ~600 token responses, bump to 6 x H100 or mix with 8 x A100-80GB depending on availability.
- KV cache: assume 20–30GB per node for session KV if sessions are reused; plan for a shared in-memory prefix cache to avoid cold-decoding on repeat templates.
- Batching: automatic continuous batching should be tuned to keep p99 latency under control; start with target batch windows of 12–25ms for chat gen.
- Token throughput estimate: rough back-of-envelope says 200 req/s * average 600 tokens -> ~120k tokens/s peak. That drives memory and NVLink saturation considerations.

Notes: this is a fast sketch — once we get the questionnaire answers and a longer (72h) trace I’ll produce a node-by-node stitch with cost/km estimates. Also will flag quantization tradeoffs if Neurolytics is open to int8 variants for the model.

— Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Porter <elliot@neurolytics.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Aug 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help for Dedicated cluster — Neurolytics pilot

Thanks Marissa & Karthik — answers below inline, and I attached an expanded 72-hour trace (sample_traffic_profile_v2.csv).

Marissa Q1: Sessions are long-lived (users keep chats open). KV cache is sticky per session and we’ll want cache reuse.
Q2: Prefix caching: ~45% of requests reuse a handful of system templates; the rest are user-unique.
Q3: Latency SLO: aim for p95 <= 600ms and p99 <= 1.2s for the pilot.
Q4: Bursts: marketing spikes expected ~3x for short campaigns, usually 30–90 minutes in duration.
Q5: Tokens in CSV are post-tokenizer for the Llama family (we tested with local tokenizer).
Q6: Yes please share the telemetry one-pager. We need 90-day retention for audit but can accept redwood’s standard 30-day operational window for live logs if longer-term retention is delivered as an export.

Timeline: we’re targeting August 20th start. We’ll sign the MSA and a short pilot addendum this week; HubSpot has the draft under deal 4392 (link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/4392).

Action items:
- I’ll upload the 72-hour trace and the filled questionnaire by EOD today.
- Please send the initial stitch & cost sketch by Friday (we need numbers for procurement).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Elliot Porter
Head of Platform — Neurolytics
